items.text: The Iranian under-17 volleyball team defeated France 3-1 in the final of the World Championship in Doha, Qatar. Iran lost the third set but won the first, second, and fourth sets. This is Iran's first championship in this tournament.

Since the beginning of 2026, the Abdul Rahman Boroumand Foundation has documented 950 executions in Iran. Among those executed are at least 20 women and 30 protesters. Additionally, 45 executions were recorded in August.
Government sources announced that popular forces have been deployed to the Strait of Hormuz. This action was taken in response to Trump's provocations. Further details have not been disclosed.

According to recorded rates on Saturday, 6 Shahrivar 1405, the US dollar price in the free market was about 205,880 tomans, and in the Herat market about 205,230 tomans. The euro was traded at about 238,910 tomans, the pound at about 279,090 tomans, and the Canadian dollar at about 148,650 tomans. Each gram of 18-karat gold was reported at about 21,810,790 tomans, and each misqal of melted gold at about 94,480,000 tomans.

Steven Miller, Deputy Chief of Staff at the White House, said Trump has achieved the most in fighting the Islamic terrorism of the Iranian government. He claimed that Iran's navy, air force, radars, and military command structure have been destroyed. Miller described this situation as the most asymmetric military achievement in modern war history.

Ali Kalateh Dolati, detained in connection with the December 2025 protests, has been held in Sabzevar prison for over 45 days without a judicial decision. His family has seen no progress in his case despite repeated follow-ups. He is also deprived of contact and visits with his family.

A video sent to Iran International shows the slogan "Long live the Shah" on a wall in Mehrshahr, Karaj. The video is from a specific location in Karaj. The slogan in this video has attracted attention.

UEFA has opened a disciplinary case against Red Star Belgrade for displaying banners honoring Ratko Mladić during a match against Viktoria Plzeň. Mladić, convicted of the Srebrenica genocide, died on Thursday. Fans held banners reading "General, eternal glory and thanks" and chanted his name during the game.

The absence of Mojtaba Khamenei continues while power gaps in the Islamic Republic have increased. Jaber Rajabi says security reasons do not sufficiently explain this absence. His absence, given his limited position, has deepened the existing void.

The Minister of Science said that during crises people become more united, but after the crisis, demands increase. He emphasized the need for social capital and development of welfare for societal resilience. He also stated that the perception of a large gap with major powers is incorrect and Iran has the ability to stand firm.

Persepolis football team defeated Malavan 3-0 in the fourth week of the Premier League. The goals were scored by Mohammad Papi (own goal), Tivi Bifuma, and Ali Alipour. Persepolis reached third place in the standings with 9 points.

Shin Bet announced that Yair Netanyahu was returned from Florida to Israel after receiving a death threat. There was a significant threat against him, and a rescue operation was carried out with the security team's cooperation. Shin Bet forces were dispatched to Miami for this operation.

Hundreds of people in Norway gathered in Oslo to pay respects during the transfer of King Harald V's coffin to the royal palace. Harald, aged 89, died after being hospitalized due to a blood infection. His son Haakon succeeded him.
Niusha Saremi discussed the dispute over Mojtaba Khamenei's new message in Titraavol. Qalibaf warned about internal disagreements. This topic was raised in the audio version of the Titraavol program.

On Saturday, 7 Shahrivar, environmental health personnel in Hamedan held a protest over unmet demands. Additionally, oil and gas workers at the Day gas field in Farashband held a protest on Thursday. These protests were held to express their grievances.

The US State Department spokesperson stated that the US stands with the people of Lebanon and calls for Hezbollah's disarmament for Lebanon's security and independence. He added that Hezbollah has so far refused to engage in talks with the Lebanese government, the US, or Israel. He also emphasized that it is time for Hezbollah to take actions that benefit Lebanon.

Abbas Rasouli-Far, a commander with experience in Syria, led the suppression forces in Shahriar during the national revolution in December 2025. A political analyst stated that the Iranian regime's response to protests has gone beyond classic suppression methods and resembles urban military operations. This pattern was previously used in the Syrian war.

The Minister of Science stated that more than 400 expelled students and 100 professors have been reinstated at universities. He described the dismissal process as "cunning" and said these individuals were removed in a way that did not officially count as expulsion. The time frame of these expulsions was not specified.

Alireza Elhami, commander of the joint air defense headquarters, stated that air defense is the top priority for the country's defense. He added that in the recent war, air defense personnel were at the forefront of countering threats. He also mentioned that Ali Khamenei issued the order to establish this headquarters in 2009.

Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and any ship passage requires coordination and permission from the Islamic Republic. Iran is in no hurry to reopen the strait and the armed forces have full oversight of movements there. The understanding between Iran and Oman on transit arrangements will not be implemented until the United States fulfills its commitments.

Duolingo announced that the institution's language test is unavailable in Iran and for holders of Iranian identity documents. At the same time, reports have been published about TOEFL test cancellations and the absence of new dates for holding it in Iran. These developments come days after OFAC suspended General License G.

Ahmad Alavi said Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks about the rising exchange rate indicate the government's attempt to evade responsibility. He added that the government has no solution to control the currency market and blames external factors. He also warned that if there are problems paying employees' salaries, the economic crisis could turn into a political crisis.

Karim Bagheri stated in a press conference after the match with Malavan that fans should be patient and only support the Persepolis team. He emphasized that it does not matter who plays, as all players serve the team.

Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh stated that there is no problem in supplying goods, but siege, war, and sanctions affect prices. The government is trying to reduce the burden of these costs on people. Global prices of essential goods and transportation costs have increased.

A Russian airstrike on an ammunition depot in Bucha resulted in at least 37 deaths. Volodymyr Zelensky criticized the storage of weapons near residential areas. A criminal investigation into possible negligence in ammunition storage has been initiated.

Abbas Mousavi stated that national power must be increased to guarantee the implementation of the agreement. He assessed the likelihood of implementing the agreement with the US through guarantees from China, Russia, or the Security Council as very low. Mousavi added that international law is now nothing more than a scrap of paper.

Maziar Zare, the head coach of Malavan football team, expelled a reporter from the Football Bartar program after the match against Persepolis. He also responded to rumors of his resignation that surfaced in the 80th minute of the game, mentioning the presence of mafia in football. Zare considered these rumors as attempts to discredit him.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in the special news program that critics of the government should provide practical plans considering the war conditions and financial limitations. He told those who demand money for their proposals that the government does not have funds. Pezeshkian also rejected claims that sanctions are ineffective.

Jalal Maleki reported an explosion of a tanker at a workshop at the beginning of Firouzbahram road. One 21-year-old worker died and two others were injured in the incident. Additionally, two small containers near the tanker caught fire.

Only two players have joined the final camp of the national U23 team for the Nagoya Asian Games. The overlap of the U23 camp with the Premier League matches has caused opposition from some league coaches. The Minister of Sports stated that clubs must release their players for the U23 team and the federation has regulations for non-compliant clubs.

Abbas Araghchi claimed that some factors in the US government are trying to manipulate the energy market using the media. These statements were made amid falling oil prices and increased commercial ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM announced that US forces have helped ensure the safe passage of nearly 1,500 ships through the Strait of Hormuz.
The audio version of the program 'Politics' with Murad Vaisi has been released. The program discusses signs of a harsh winter and the risk of famine. It was broadcast by Iran International.

Mehdi Moslehi said that Iraq's oil exports via Turkey have limited short-term impact but can reduce Iraq's dependence on the Strait of Hormuz in the long term. Developing this route strengthens Iraq's energy security but requires resolving security and political obstacles. Until these challenges are addressed, the Strait of Hormuz remains Iraq's main oil export route.

Navid Mohibi said that Prince Reza Pahlavi's emphasis on unity, discipline, and responsibility is a response to recent opposition disputes. He added that no successful political movement should allow personal differences to overshadow the main struggle. Also, the statement by royalist political prisoners shows an emphasis on common principles for convergence.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said Iran is gradually moving from modern famine to classic famine and real shortages of essential goods. Experts warn that gasoline shortages may also affect food supplies. This crisis is the result of incompetence, corruption, and plundering by the Islamic Republic officials.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, described the return of some critics to Iran as a project directed by the Islamic Republic's intelligence agencies. He stated that this process cannot be viewed merely as a right of return. He also referred to the blood of the victims of the December uprising, which he associates with this project.

Reza Pahlavi expressed gratitude for the statement of 160 political prisoners and their families. He emphasized the need for unity and avoiding peripheral disagreements to save Iran. This message was in response to the statement by monarchist political prisoners and activists inside the country.

The US government has made a new decision to intensify sanctions against the Islamic Republic, which will make it difficult for Iranian students to participate in international exams such as TOEFL or GRE. The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the US Treasury Department announced that General License J, which since 2014 allowed the provision of educational and academic services to Iranians, has been suspended "indefinitely" as of August 23. This suspension means that American companies can no longer provide services related to university entrance and professional certification exams to Iranians.

Maryam Saeedpour was named Fine Arts Photographer of the Year at the 2026 International Photography Awards for her series "Painful Embrace." The series is a personal depiction of wartime in Tehran expressing fear and a desire for peace. Saeedpour will receive a $1,000 prize and compete for the International Photographer of the Year title.

Hassan Beigdeli spoke at a pro-government gathering in Zanjan, stating that the country is under war, sanctions, and pressure, and people should be aware of this reality. He emphasized the need to discuss saving and cooperation but warned against creating a sense of weakness in society. Beigdeli also highlighted the importance of expressing the country's military, economic, and industrial capabilities.

Hossein Samsami, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, stated that Iran's economy has not yet been affected by the 180,000 toman exchange rate and a more severe inflation wave is expected. He equated free transactions between exporters and importers to allowing smuggled dollars. He also predicted that the exchange rate of 204 to 205 thousand tomans will impact people's livelihoods and lead to permanent inflation.

Anwar Gargash, the UAE foreign policy advisor, stated that the UAE stands firmly with the just cause of the Palestinians. He also said the UAE opposes exploiting this issue to fuel extremism and violence. The UAE has long provided a refuge and opportunities for a dignified life, security, and stability for Palestinians.

Mojtaba Khamenei emphasized in a message for Unity Week that the real enemy of Islamic countries must be recognized and confronted. He stated that Islam has reached a decisive stage and that the enemy seeks to divide the Islamic community. He also said that the rulers of the US and Israel are enemies of the entire Islamic community.

Hossein Simaei-Sarraf, the Minister of Science, announced that more than 400 expelled students and 100 expelled professors have returned to universities. Mehrdad Mohammadi stated that universities have become places for political personnel shifts. The Ministry of Science should announce the names of the returned individuals.

During the February 11, 2026 rally, a statue referred to as "Baal" by organizers was set on fire. Salar Velayatmadar, a parliamentary representative, stated that the publication of Mojtaba Khamenei's image was stopped on the advice of religious scholars and security officials. These statements indicate the official security narrative has incorporated occult sciences.

Meysam Mehrani stated that Iraqi armed groups have committed to stopping operations, but real disarmament requires handing over all equipment and arsenals. These groups have influence in parliament and the Popular Mobilization Forces structure, and the Iraqi government has adopted a gradual process for disarmament. The government's current focus is on stopping the operations of these groups.

Abdolhossein Hemmati, a member of the Energy Commission of the Parliament, said the global oil and gas market is facing risks in production and transportation. European countries need more gas and LNG supplies as winter approaches. Any disruption in gas exports from the Persian Gulf could lead to price increases.

Roozbeh Boualheri from Iran International stated that workers face increasing layoffs, low wages, and high living costs. The living cost for a household is about 90 million tomans, while the minimum wage for a married worker with one child is about 24 million tomans. Government promises to increase wages or ration cards are insufficient to bridge this gap.

Hamidreza Haji Babaei stated that the US does not want the Iranian people to have a good life and opposes Iran. He added that the US fears Iran becoming a superpower. He also emphasized that Iran does not seek war but will respond if attacked.

Israel's internal security agency confirmed the immediate transfer of Yair Netanyahu from the US to Israel due to threats against his life. Yair Netanyahu was targeted in an assassination plot by the Islamic Republic last December. A Middle East history researcher described this as part of a new phase of proxy terrorism by the Islamic Republic against Jews.

Ali Shirazi commented on Mojtaba Khamenei's message about the unity of Muslim countries against the US and Israel. He said this stance contradicts the Islamic Republic's actions in the 40-day war. Muslim countries in the region were targeted by Iran's attacks, and only proxy groups affiliated with the Islamic Republic supported it.
The Tehran Police Information Center announced the arrest of a citizen for sending news and information to some foreign media outlets.

A group of Iranians living in Sweden gathered in Gothenburg on Saturday, 7th of Shahrivar. They protested against the Islamic Republic and shouted "Long live the Shah." This event was recorded in videos received by Iran International.

The Israeli energy minister mentioned the possibility of another attack on the Islamic Republic if nuclear facilities are rebuilt. Israel reserves the right to preemptive military action and does not consider a potential Tehran-Washington agreement as a guarantee of its security. According to Israel, the agreement must limit Iran's nuclear technical capabilities.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, said the enemy will not stop until the religion is overthrown and that resistance with full power is necessary. He emphasized that yielding and giving in to the enemy's demands does not end the conflict. According to him, the more is given, the more pressure the enemy will apply.
A citizen stated in a video that he went to three fuel stations to buy gasoline, but all were closed. He blamed the Islamic Republic officials for causing war and poverty among the people.

Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen stated that if the Islamic Republic attempts to rebuild its nuclear or missile programs, Israel will attack again. He emphasized that Israel's military action will take place regardless of any potential agreement between Tehran and Washington. This report was provided by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.
Reza Amani Far and Asghar Hajeb, two teacher activists in Bushehr province, were summoned to court in separate cases.

Inter Miami defeated Montreal 7-1 in the 22nd week of the US league. Lionel Messi played a key role with 4 goals and one assist. With this victory, Inter Miami reduced their gap to the top of the table to 10 points.

Ali Zeynivand, the spokesperson of the Ministry of Interior, said that the blockade affects Iran but does not only harm its economy. He emphasized that Iran is not defenseless and will respond strongly. He also stated that a complete blockade of Iran is impossible due to its many borders and various transfer routes.

Since early Shahrivar, the salaries of Qazvin University of Medical Sciences staff have not been fully paid. Gas stations in Mashhad have not recharged free fuel cards, and free fuel distribution has been halted. Ghadir Petrochemical Company has shut down due to the closure of Arvand Petrochemical, and power and water outages continue in Shahr-e Qods, Tehran.

Islam Azarian, a resident of Dehdasht, was arrested by security forces in late August. He is currently held in Dehdasht prison facing charges of propaganda against the regime and insulting the leadership. His situation in prison remains uncertain.

Abolfazl Aboutorabi, the representative of Najafabad, stated that Iran has no assets from the US but can seize assets of Arab countries and US allies. He cited Article 2 of the UN Charter, emphasizing that countries aiding the US are also subject to this action. Aboutorabi mentioned Bulgaria and Cyprus as countries whose assets might be seized.

Access to the international Duolingo test has been cut off for users inside Iran and holders of Iranian identification cards due to US sanctions. This occurred following the intensification of sanctions. More details were provided in an interview with Ali Rashid.

The first branch of the Revolutionary Court in Isfahan sentenced 10 protesters from the December protests in the Shohada Square case to death. Other defendants received long prison sentences. Additionally, a female defendant's complaint about assault during detention was not addressed.

The Jerusalem Post reported on Sunday that Greece is set to sign a $3.6 billion defense deal with Israel. The agreement will equip Athens with an integrated multi-layered defense system to counter potential aerial threats from the Islamic Republic and Turkey.

Yesterday, several Saipa customers held a protest in front of the company's building in Tehran. The protest was due to contract changes and demands for additional payments by the company. Customers expressed their objections to this issue.

The price of some types of sanitary pads in Iran has increased more than fivefold over the past year. The brand My Lady has risen by 330% to 165,000 tomans, and Tafteh has increased by 430% to 112,000 tomans. Imported brands are also sold for up to 600,000 tomans.

The Iranian women's national volleyball team finished fourth in the 2026 Asian Championship after losing to Japan in the third-place match. Iran lost in three consecutive sets and missed out on a medal. For the first time, the team reached the semifinals and ultimately secured fourth place.

Esteghlal Club expressed concern about the incidents during the match against Foolad Khuzestan and announced an official complaint to the judicial bodies of the Football Federation. The club reported threats and insulting slogans against its players and fans. They also reported throwing bottles and fireworks onto the field, endangering the players' safety.

Iman Aghayari said the father of the absent leader of the Islamic Republic could not establish himself as the leader of the Muslim world. He added that few Muslim leaders attended his funeral. Therefore, addressing Muslim leaders by Mojtaba Khamenei is an illusion.
A student referred to the rising inflation in Iran in a video. He described the situation as the "masterpiece blunder of the Islamic Republic." The video was sent to Iran International.

The Israeli prosecutor's office announced indictments against two teenagers aged 14 and 16 for cooperating with the Islamic Republic. They are accused of photographing, transferring information, and recruiting minors for missions of the Islamic Republic. The indictment has been submitted to the Haifa juvenile court.

A video shows a group of men and women performing a local dance in Qeytarieh Park, Tehran, on the evening of Friday, 6th of Shahrivar. They are holding hands while dancing. The video was received by Iran International.

Israeli police have taken legal action against two teenagers aged 14 and 16 for espionage and carrying out missions for the Iranian government. The teenagers were recruited via Telegram in June and performed missions in exchange for money. The person who recruited them claimed to be connected to the Islamic Republic.

Arash Azarmi referred to the statements of Masoud Pezeshkian's deputy about the organized fuel smuggling in Iran. He said daily smuggling of 20 to 30 million liters of fuel is not done in small scale and there is evidence of its organized nature. He added that fuel smuggling generates five to eight billion dollars annually and is an example of corruption and plundering of the country's oil resources.

Ali Hashemi, a detainee from the December protests, died in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. His family, after a week of no news, learned he was hospitalized due to cardiac arrest but found his lifeless body at the hospital. At the same time, the family of Erfan Esfandiari mourned at his 40th-day memorial.

The acting head of Qazvin University of Medical Sciences reported a severe shortage of dialysis beds in the province. The treatment standard is one bed per four patients, but in Qazvin, this ratio has reached one bed per seven patients. He suggested solutions such as completing hospital projects and opening the Mohammadzadeh dialysis center.

Mohsen Mahdian stated that reducing the hostility of the US towards the Islamic Republic to the nuclear issue and enrichment is simplistic. He added that enrichment is a symbol of hostility, not the essence of it.
A citizen in Gilan province says the electricity in their city is cut off for up to six hours a day. He compared this situation to the Stone Age. This report was sent to Iran International.

Mohammad Kazem Anbarlouei, deputy secretary-general of the Islamic Coalition Party, stated that the country's progress path cannot be paved by compromise and that the enemy must be defeated. He added that the claim of progress through the path set by the US is incorrect. The country's path should follow the guidance and policies of Imam Noor, Khamenei.

In the Iranian bodybuilding championship, the memory of Masoud Zatparvar was honored. He was a world classic physique champion and bodybuilding coach. Zatparvar was killed on January 8, 2026, during the Iranian national revolution in Rasht.

A citizen sent a video showing the release of a white balloon in memory of Majid Adineh, an executed protester. Majid Adineh was arrested on January 9, 2026, and executed on August 23, 2026. His execution was ordered by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj.

The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was launched into space by a Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center. Its main five-year mission is to study dark energy and dark matter and to identify thousands of exoplanets. This news was reported by Iran International.

The Court of Appeal of West Azerbaijan Province sentenced 29 citizens of Piranshahr to pay 20 million tomans each as a fine instead of three months imprisonment. These individuals had previously faced legal action due to the release of a video showing dancing at a wedding ceremony.

Mehr news agency reported that since August 22, 30 unauthorized vessels attempted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz but were stopped by the Islamic Republic's armed forces. Passage through the approved route is limited and requires coordination and payment of fees. Before the war, over 1,500 oil tankers and 1,700 commercial ships had passed through this route.

Reuters reported that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent intends to pressure G20 member countries to increase pressure on Tehran, including cutting trade ties with the Islamic Republic. Reuters wrote that the US Treasury Secretary wants to put Tehran at the center of attention and talk about tightening sanctions. The meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors will be held on Monday and Tuesday.
A citizen sent a video showing a dust storm near the city of Sahneh in Kermanshah province. The event occurred on Sunday, the 8th of Shahrivar. The video was published by Iran International.

Mojtaba Maleki, head of the Bodybuilding Federation, identified Masoud Zatparvar as one of the agitators of last December and condemned the act. He apologized to the families of the martyrs and those hurt by the incident. The federation will fully cooperate with legal authorities to identify those responsible for organizing the ceremony.

A citizen succeeded in getting a PhD admission in the US after three years of effort. However, he faced the Trump administration's ban on Iranian entry to the US. Also, with Iranian identification documents, it is not possible to take TOEFL and Duolingo tests, and the IELTS test is not held in Iran.

Russia is planning a new ground attack on Kyiv amid ongoing missile and drone strikes. Concerns have increased about the possibility of NATO countries being targeted. The Russian military command has been tasked with preparing several scenarios for operations in northern Ukraine, with Kyiv and Chernihiv as main focuses.

Ashkan Nezamabadi said China dealt the biggest blow to the Islamic Republic in the energy market. China forced refineries to store oil and used its reserves. These actions prevented oil prices from reaching $200, and alternative oil routes remain operational.

The Tabriz Civil Registration Office has opposed naming a boy "Berkay." The child, born on 6 Bahman 1404, has been without a birth certificate for over seven months. The opposition is due to the name "Berkay" not being registered in the office's system.

Asghar Hajeb, a board member of the Bushehr Teachers' Union, has been summoned again to the Revolutionary Court. He was arrested in May by security forces and released on bail. He is accused of propaganda against the regime and must appear in court on September 1.

Images sent to Iran International show the critical and poor condition of prisoners in Isfahan Central Prison. At least 400 detainees of the Iranian National Revolution are held there without access to lawyers or family visits. This information was reported by the audience and Iran International.

Mark Fife, former US national security advisor, told Al Jazeera that China has reduced its daily oil imports from Iran from 1.5 million barrels to 500,000 barrels and has turned to buying from Brazil, Iraq, and Russia to meet its oil needs.

The Washington Post reported that senior US military officials warned Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth that continued large-scale operations against the Islamic Republic are unsustainable and weaken the US military's ability to counter other threats. The warnings were given in a secret document dated August 14, and senior commanders registered non-concurrence with the order to extend deployment but will execute it.

The Washington Post reported that senior US military officials warned Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth that continued large-scale military operations against Iran are unsustainable and weaken the military's ability to counter other threats. The warnings were recorded in a secret document, and commanders expressed non-concurrence with extending troop deployments. CENTCOM has kept over 50,000 troops on alert, and some deployments have been extended until 2027.

Pouria Shahrabadi, Danial Eiri, and Pouria Latififar have been added to the Iran U23 football team camp. The U23 team is preparing for the Asian competitions and will play its first match on September 16 in Nagoya against the UAE. They are in a group with the UAE, North Korea, and China.

Zahra Mousavi, arrested during the December 2025 protests, is imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. She has been sentenced to a total of 10 years and six months in prison, with four years to be served and six years and six months suspended. This sentence was issued by the Revolutionary Court.

The head of the Civil Registration Organization announced that the smart national ID cards of 6 million Iranian citizens have not yet been issued and delivered. He attributed this to inflation of laws and multiple responsible agencies. He also mentioned that significant improvements will be made regarding the photos on the ID cards.

Iranians residing in Berlin held a protest gathering and raised the Lion and Sun flag. They carried images of those who died in the protests and emphasized keeping their memory alive. The protesters demanded the expulsion of Islamic Republic diplomats from Germany.
Nemat Elhami, a candidate for the twelfth parliamentary elections from Parsabad, Bileh Savar, and Aslanduz, suddenly suffered cardiac arrest and died during a nighttime rally speech.

Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that he will refill the US strategic national reserve with Venezuelan oil, calling the reserves empty due to Joe Biden's performance. He said the process of completing these reserves will begin soon and considered it a gift from Venezuela to the American people.

Donald Trump announced that Venezuelan oil will be used to fill the United States' strategic reserves. He described this action as a gift from the people of Venezuela to the people of the United States. The process of filling the reserves will begin soon.

Mehrdad Goodarzvand Chegini, deputy head of the Parliament's Budget and Planning Commission, emphasized expanding barter trade with neighboring countries and using national currencies in trade to gradually phase out the dollar. He cited Qatar as a successful example and stated the goal is to increase the presence of Iranian goods and services in regional and global markets. Defense, oil and gas, and medical and engineering services are among Iran's export capacities.

The Tabriz Civil Registration Office has refused to issue a birth certificate for a boy named 'Berkay' more than seven months after his birth. The parents' complaints against the registration office were rejected by the peace courts in Tabriz. The family presented another birth certificate with the same name to the court, but the registration office stated it belonged to a different person.

Behzad Akbari stated that more than 30 percent of the world's most visited domains are blocked for Iranian users. The Infrastructure Communications Company monitors access to about 700,000 domains around the clock. This statistic does not include internal filtering in Iran, which worsens the situation.

The Yemeni naval forces seized a boat carrying drone parts from the Islamic Republic that was heading to the Houthis. The Yemeni National Resistance has released images of these parts. This incident took place on the western coast of Yemen.

A citizen reported that the Iranian estradiol pill, prescribed to compensate for estrogen deficiency, has become scarce. He had to obtain the foreign version at a high cost. This issue was reported in a video to Iran International.

Greece and Israel will sign a $3.5 billion agreement on Monday to establish the "Achilles Shield" air and missile defense network. The plan is designed to counter hostile drones, missiles, and aircraft.

Mojtaba Khamenei called for Gulf countries to unite with Iran against the US and Israel. Israel's energy minister warned that if Iran resumes its missile and nuclear programs, Israel will attack Iran. This report was provided by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

Omid Pourfathollah, a detainee from the December 2025 protests, was sentenced by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court to 12 years, six months, and one day in prison. Five years of this sentence have been suspended. His charges include forming a group aimed at disrupting security and propaganda against the regime.

Saeed Jalili stated that the idea of resolving issues through negotiation must be corrected and deterrence occurs when the opponent knows their actions will not go unanswered. He emphasized the need to maximize the use of the Strait of Hormuz's capacity. Jalili also mentioned that war is not limited to the military domain but includes economic, political, media, and security areas.

The Lebanese Foreign Ministry stated that the Islamic Republic must pursue its relations with Lebanon through official and legal institutions and should not independently engage with internal parties. The ministry welcomed Tehran's desire to maintain good relations with the Lebanese government. Lebanon also emphasized that relations must be conducted through governments and respect for sovereignty must be observed.

Mehdi Moslehi said the US is implementing a long-term strategy by limiting Iran's oil exports and protecting the passage of Arab oil tankers. He added that Iran has lost a large part of its oil market and leverage over the Strait of Hormuz. The relative calm in the oil market indicates traders do not expect a complete halt in regional oil exports.

The deputy of primary education in North Khorasan's education department announced the identification of 1304 children out of school in the province. So far, 442 of these children have been enrolled in schools. The status of the remaining 862 children is still being followed up.

Shayan Samiei explained the US effort to involve G20 countries in economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He said the key point is the decision of banks, shipping companies, and global insurers to continue or stop cooperation with Tehran. Cooperation with the Islamic Republic could jeopardize their access to the US financial system.
